## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useVueConsistentVForDelimiter`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has a [**safe**](/linter/#safe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/v-for-delimiter-style`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/v-for-delimiter-style)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useVueConsistentVForDelimiter": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Enforce a consistent delimiter between the item and the list in `v-for` directives.

In a `v-for` directive, Vue accepts both `in` and `of` between the item and the
list, and treats them the same way: `item in items` and `item of items` render
the same list. Using the same word everywhere makes templates easier to read
and search.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <div v-for="item of items"></div>
</template>
```

### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <div v-for="item in items"></div>
  <div v-for="(item, index) in items"></div>
</template>
```

## Options

### `delimiter`

The word to use between the item and the list: `"in"` or `"of"`.

Default: `"in"`

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useVueConsistentVForDelimiter": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"delimiter": "of"
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

#### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <div v-for="item in items"></div>
</template>
```
